evidence: Cic. Off. 1.59: addendō dēdūcendōque vidēre, quae reliquī summa fīat
terms.comment: Latin names the operation with the verb, often the gerund: addendō dēdūcendōque, by adding and subtracting (Cic. Off. 1.59). The result is the summa.

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation (-iō), with the dative or ad
terms.comment: Traupman’s word in his school vocabulary; subtract is dētrahō (Traupman 32).

phrases.latin: ut bonī ratiōcinātōrēs officiōrum esse possīmus et addendō dēdūcendōque vidēre, quae reliquī summa fīat
phrases.english: so that we may keep good accounts of our duties and, by adding and subtracting, see what the balance comes to

sources: Lewis & Short: addo · Lewis & Short: adjicio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 28, 32, 268.
Cicero, De officiis 1, checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (9 November 2026).
